newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes, Brent paper steady in thin talk.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes, Brent paper steady in thin talk.

text.p: North Sea crudes and Brent paper values were broadly unchanged in early talk on Thursday but West African grades looked perkier as evidence began to emerge of active trade earlier in the week, traders said.
June Brent shed three cents to $17.78 a barrel by 1047 GMT while intermonth spreads were unchanged with June/July moving at -19 cents.

Brent Contracts for Difference (CFDs) were steady, next week's dates changing hands at June Brent -59 cents, broadly in line with late Wednesday talk. Only one May 2-4 Brent cargo was due to turn wet on Thursday, traders said.
"It's been another quiet morning. It wouldn't surprise me if directionally things were starting to improve but we're waiting for the evidence to back that up," said a trader.
Talk of two early May Forties cargoes trading on Wednesday could not be confirmed but traders said with first decade supply looking thin, differentials could start to move higher.
While North Sea activity was slow, traders reported a brisker pace on West African markets earlier in the week.
European refiners were seen picking up Nigerian Bonny Light/Medium and Forcados while a late May Angolan Palanca found a home in Asia.
A European major picked up two Bonny Light/Medium combinations in the May 1-20 period while there were unconfirmed reports of a Japanese refiner taking a Bonny Light/Forcados VLCC loading May 15-25.
Bonny Light was pegged a couple of cents firmer at Dated Brent +25/+30 cents while Forcados picked up about five cents to talk around Dated Brent -20 cents.
A South Korean refiner was reported to have taken a Palanca/Bonny Light combination loading in the second half of May, traders said.
